answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
We support rigorous carbon accounting standards that help market participants reduce real-world emissions, and we understand the intended purpose of the consequential accounting proposal. We are, however, concerned that the proposal introduces risks, ambiguities, and unintended outcomes that run counter to its goals. Power-system modeling is inherently complex, dependent on forward-looking assumptions, and even sophisticated outlooks can diverge from actual grid behavior. As drafted, the proposal could result in reported ‘avoided emissions’ that are neither comparable across companies nor credibly additional to baseline market outcomes.
We are in favor of a rigorous accounting methodology based on measurable, verifiable data on our own operations rather than impacts that rely on forward looking predictions of system-wide effects of an individual project. The estimation methodologies provided within the consequential analysis are not aligned with accounting principles around accuracy and comparability. We are supportive of incrementality, which will be driven by the reporting proposal with the combination of deliverability, temporal accounting and SSS. We recommend additional refinement of the SSS definition and application to ensure it is structured to drive true incrementality and the intention is well understood.

audit_basis: A listed oil and gas company filed in the Fossil fuels sector.
